rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 report the authors' own ISAREG model runs for 2001-2003 daily data and 1970-2003 10-day series, built on their own field experiments at the Azizbek-1 farm (Fig. 1 compares observed vs simulated soil water). Q2: Section 2.1 and Tables 7-13: the model uses FAO56 (Allen et al. 1998) Kc-ETo methodology and is used to search improved full and deficit schedules to cope with water scarcity, reporting water savings, RYL, WP and EWP; Fig. 1 shows good agreement of simulated and observed soil water and Section 3.2.3 says simulated yields agree with field-measured ones. Q4: Tables 6-8, 10-12 and Figs. 4-6 report the intermediate water-balance terms (deep percolation, ASW, groundwater contribution, ETa/ETc) through which the schedules deliver savings. Q7: Section 3.2.3 end and Section 3.3.3/Conclusions state from results that water saving strategies require improved farm irrigation systems allowing the preferred depths and improved delivery schedules and furrow performance. Q8: Section 3.1 notes the daily-data years 2001-2003 are low-demand/wet years (2003 the most humid of the series); Section 3.2.3 notes simulated WP is slightly higher than field values because larger depths were applied in field studies; Conclusions note the first dataset refers to wet years.
rows.notes: Single site, single crop, simulation-only (one method); no scheme/district-scale results; no SD/CI or uncertainty propagation reported (frequency distribution of NIR across years is not dispersion of the claimed scheduling result). Calibration/validation detail is largely in the companion paper Eholpankulov et al. (2008), but Fig. 1 here presents the observed-simulated comparison.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a model application (ISAREG, FAO56-based) validated against the authors' own field soil-water observations; the claim passage cites it merely as an example of such application, which the study directly is.
